 By Tom Kao November 11, 2026 With its mix of romance, espionage and political intrigue, "100 Days of Deception" has plenty to keep viewers hooked. Starring Kim You-jung and Park Jinyoung, the series follows a skilled pickpocket who goes undercover for Korea's independence movement in 1930s Gyeongseong, only to find herself caught up with a mysterious interpreter working for the Japanese colonial government. If you've been enjoying the secrets, suspense and unexpected romance, here are five other period K-dramas worth adding to your watchlist 
 Mr. Sunshine (2018)
 Set in the early 1900s, Mr. Sunshine follows Eugene Choi (Lee Byung-hun), a boy born into slavery who escapes to America and eventually returns to Korea as a US Marine officer. Despite holding resentment towards his homeland, he finds himself falling for Go Ae-sin (Kim Tae-ri), a noblewoman who secretly leads a double life as a sniper for the Righteous Army. But with Japan's influence over Korea growing stronger, their romance becomes caught up in the country's fight for independence. Expect a sweeping love story filled with political intrigue, hidden identities and plenty of emotional moments.
 Song of the Bandits (2023)
 If the independence movement storyline caught your attention, Song of the Bandits should definitely be on your radar. Set in the lawless region of Gando during the 1920s, the series follows Lee Yoon (Kim Nam-gil), a former Japanese military soldier who leaves his past behind and joins a group of bandits protecting Korean settlers. Along the way, he crosses paths with Nam Hee-shin (Seohyun), who secretly supports the independence movement while working for the Japanese colonial government. With its Western-inspired action, undercover missions and conflicting loyalties, there's plenty of tension to keep things interesting.

 Gyeongseong Creature (2023)
 For those who prefer something a little darker, Gyeongseong Creature adds a terrifying twist to the historical drama genre. Set in 1945, it follows Jang Tae-sang (Park Seo-jun), a wealthy pawnshop owner who must track down a missing woman or risk losing everything. He teams up with Yoon Chae-ok (Han So-hee), a skilled investigator searching for her long-lost mother. Their search soon leads them to Ongseong Hospital, where horrifying experiments and a deadly creature await. Throw in a developing romance, and you've got a gripping mix of horror, mystery and historical drama.
 Chicago Typewriter (2017)
 Historical drama meets fantasy and romance in Chicago Typewriter , which takes viewers between modern-day Korea and the 1930s. The story centres on bestselling author Han Se-joo (Yoo Ah-in), whose struggle with writer's block takes an unexpected turn when a mysterious typewriter and ghostwriter enter his life. Together with Jeon Seol (Im Soo-jung), he begins uncovering their connections to Korea's independence movement in their past lives. As their forgotten memories gradually resurface, a story of love, friendship and betrayal unfolds, making this a great pick for anyone who enjoys a little mystery with their historical romance.
 Snowdrop (2021)
 Taking us forward to 1987, Snowdrop stars Blackpink's Jisoo as Eun Yeong-ro, a university student who secretly takes in an injured man, Im Soo-ho (Jung Hae-in), believing he's a student protester on the run. However, things take a dramatic turn when she discovers that he's actually a North Korean spy, pulling them both into a dangerous political conspiracy and hostage crisis. As feelings begin to grow between them, their relationship becomes increasingly complicated by secrets and divided loyalties. If forbidden romance and political intrigue are what you enjoy, this one's worth watching.
